# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says the wires must be cut in order: purple, blue, then green. However, Deaf must first establish the gesture code, and my opening move is to wait for that code.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Gesture code: thumbs up means YES; thumbs down means NO; OK hand means HOLD; raised palm means DONE. I will now show them in that order.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍 👎 👌 ✋]

The manual gives a three-item ordered instruction, which cannot yet be expressed using only YES, NO, HOLD, and DONE. I should signal HOLD so Deaf knows the code must be expanded before transmitting the instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Please read the manual now. Keep using the established code: thumbs up YES, thumbs down NO, OK HOLD, raised palm DONE. For a digit, use: index up 0, index down 1, point left 2, point right 3, victory 4, horns 5, open hand 6, raised palm 7, crossed fingers 8, horns-rock 9. Signal the manual's required action to me.

The established code can transmit digits, but it has no mapping for wire colors. I cannot safely translate purple, blue, and green into digits without Deaf first defining a color code, so I signal HOLD rather than risk an ambiguous instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✋]

The manual’s required values are wire colors, but the current code only provides control words and digits. Deaf’s DONE signal does not establish any mapping for purple, blue, or green, so I must request that the code be expanded for colors.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The color names still have no established encoding in the shared code. Deaf’s YES only confirms receipt; it does not define how to represent purple, blue, or green. I must continue holding until a color mapping is established.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Your repeated OK gesture is read as HOLD. Please now transmit the manual's complete verdict: use exactly YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE as applicable, and if an action is required, encode its full instruction with the established digit gestures. Do not merely acknowledge.

The manual requires a specific three-color sequence. The established code has no color or wire-identity mapping, so the complete instruction cannot be encoded with the available digit gestures. I must signal HOLD rather than inventing a meaning for digits.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual still requires transmitting three wire colours in order, and the established code contains no symbols for colours. Since the instruction does not fit the current code, I signal HOLD again rather than assigning unsupported meanings to the digit gestures.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎]

Deaf’s NO does not provide a color encoding or make the three required wire identities transmittable. The instruction still does not fit the established code, so I continue to request expansion rather than send an unsafe digit sequence.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I read your OK gesture as HOLD. If the manual has no further instruction, signal DONE with raised palm; otherwise continue sending the required instruction.

The manual has further instruction: cut purple, then blue, then green. The current code still lacks mappings for those wire colours, so DONE would be false and a digit sequence would be ambiguous. I signal HOLD to require the needed code expansion.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Answer this question using one gesture only: does the manual currently require HOLD? Use thumbs up for YES or thumbs down for NO. Do not use OK hand.

The manual does not require the HOLD verdict; it requires the concrete action sequence of cutting purple, blue, then green. Therefore the answer is NO.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Answer one question with exactly one gesture: does the manual require operating the KEYPAD? Use thumbs up for YES or thumbs down for NO.

The manual specifies cutting three wires and says nothing about operating a keypad. The answer is NO.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 12
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Answer one question with exactly one gesture: does the manual require operating the WIRES? Use thumbs up for YES or thumbs down for NO.

The manual explicitly requires cutting wires, so it does require operating the wires. The answer is YES.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
